text:
# SEO and GEO audit: Atlas (Remix)

I read all 10 tracked files. I did not run the app, so these findings come from the source only.

## High severity

1. **`public/robots.txt:5-6` blocks Bingbot.**
   - `Disallow: /` for Bingbot removes the site from Bing. ChatGPT search, Copilot and DuckDuckGo depend on Bing's index.
   - It also contradicts `geo.config.json:1`, which sets `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
   - Fix: delete the Bingbot block.

2. **`app/routes/changelog.tsx:4-6` renders its content only on the client.**
   - Entries load in `useEffect` from `/api/changelog`, so the server HTML has an empty `<ul>`.
   - Most AI crawlers don't run JavaScript, so they see no content.
   - Fix: use a Remix `loader` and `useLoaderData` so the entries are in the server HTML. No `/api/changelog` route exists in the repo either, so confirm that endpoint is real.

3. **`app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` has no `meta` export.**
   - The page has no title, no description and no canonical link.
   - The content is also thin: "Talk to us for a quote" gives crawlers and AI answers no plan names or prices.
   - Fix: add `meta` with a title, description and canonical `https://atlasroadmaps.example/pricing`. Publish plan names and prices as real text, and add `Offer` or `Product` JSON-LD.

## Medium severity

4. **`public/robots.txt:8-9` blocks only GPTBot, so the training-crawler policy is only partly enforced.**
   - `geo.config.json:1` says `trainingCrawlers: "block"`, but other training crawlers fall under `User-agent: *` and are allowed.
   - Fix: add `Disallow: /` for `CCBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `Google-Extended`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Bytespider` and `meta-externalagent`.
   - Also add explicit `Allow: /` entries for `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `PerplexityBot`, `Claude-SearchBot` and `Claude-User`, so the intent is clear and stays safe if the wildcard rule changes.

5. **`public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line.** Add `Sitemap: https://atlasroadmaps.example/sitemap.xml`.

6. **`app/root.tsx:2` sets only a generic title and description.**
   - The title is just "Atlas", and the root `meta` sets no `og:*` or `twitter:*` tags and no canonical link.
   - Fix: add `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url`, `og:type` and `twitter:card`. The same tags are missing from every route.

7. **No structured data anywhere.**
   - There is no `Organization`, `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage` or `Offer` JSON-LD.
   - Fix: add `Organization` and `SoftwareApplication` in `app/root.tsx` and `Offer` data on the pricing page, via a `<script type="application/ld+json">`.

8. **Thin content on `app/routes/_index.tsx:7-9` and `app/routes/features.tsx:2`.**
   - Both pages are a heading plus one sentence.
   - `_index.tsx:8` says "Integrates with all the tools you already use" without naming a single tool, so there is nothing for an AI answer to cite.
   - Fix: add concrete, extractable facts: named integrations, feature descriptions, and a short FAQ or "what is Atlas" paragraph in plain prose.

## Low severity

9. **`app/routes/_index.tsx:9` uses a `<div onClick>` for navigation.**
   - Crawlers can't follow it, and it isn't keyboard-accessible.
   - The features page is also not linked from the home page or from the nav in `app/root.tsx:7`.
   - Fix: use `<Link to="/features">` or `<a href="/features">`, and add Features to the nav.

10. **`app/root.tsx:7` is missing Features in the nav, and the nav has no `<header>` or `aria-label`.** The Features page is reachable only through the sitemap and the `div` above.

11. **`public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has no `<lastmod>` values.** Add them, especially for the changelog.

12. **No `llms.txt` and no `public/favicon`.** An `llms.txt` is optional, but a short one summarising the product and key URLs is cheap. Add a favicon via `links` in `root.tsx`.

13. **Short meta descriptions (`root.tsx:2`, `_index.tsx:2`).** Expand them to about 120–160 characters. The root description also duplicates the `<h1>` on the home page.

## Checked and fine
- `app/routes/dashboard.tsx:1` has `noindex`, and `robots.txt:3` blocks `/dashboard`, which is consistent. One caveat: a robots.txt `Disallow` stops crawlers from ever seeing the `noindex` tag, so a URL linked from elsewhere can still be indexed. Keep only one of the two mechanisms, and prefer `noindex` alone if the page must stay out of results.
- `<html lang="en">` is set.
- Canonical links and sitemap URLs are consistent for the home, features and changelog pages.

I made no changes to the repo.
